newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Relief agency slams U.N. delays over Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Relief agency slams U.N. delays over Zaire.

text.p: The head of CARE International has criticised the U.N. Security Council over its delay in deploying an international peace force in central Africa where hundreds of thousands face starvation.
Paul Thyness, in Hanoi for the non-governmental agency's annual meeting, said decisive U.N. action to protect refugees in eastern Zaire and ensure relief supplies is essential.

"CARE International considers the need for decisive action by the United Nations to be imperative and any delay to be unacceptable," he said in a letter to U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali.

A copy of the letter, faxed to Reuters on Monday, said CARE International was "deeply concerned" by a U.N. Security Council decision to delay consideration of the deployment of an international force until November 20.
He urged that a multinational force be deployed immediately force to secure, temporary safe havens for refugees and supply corridors for the movement of relief to these areas.
CARE is the world's largest, non-sectarian, non-governmental international relief and development agency.
The Security Council early called on U.N. members on Saturday to lay the groundwork for an international force to help end the crisis in eastern Zaire but postponed its deployment.

The interim resolution, adopted unanimously, asked the states involved to report back as soon as possible to enable the council to give final approval. Boutros-Ghali wasked to report to the council by November 20.
A U.N. official in Burundi was quoted as saying on Sunday the refugees "will all be dead by the time the U.N. makes up its mind what to do".
Fighting in eastern Zaire has spread death, fear and misery across a vast stretch of the biggest country in Central Africa.

About one million Rwandan Hutu refugees are in eastern Zaire where they fled after the genocide of up to one million minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus. For the past two years the majority have refused to go home, fearing reprisals.
